summary: Per explicit human authorization following Phase 146E's VERIFIED verdict, produced a complete implementation plan for CHGR-REQ-194 through CHGR-REQ-209 (CHGR-001 v1.2 Sec.26/Sec.28). Independently reconstructed the required implementation from primary sources rather than restating any prior phase's own summary: CHGR-001 Sec.26/Sec.28 read in full (all judgment calls, the Migration Strategy, the Regression and Compatibility reviews); the current implementation read directly (src/pcae/governance/publication/record.py, coordinator.py, storage.py; src/pcae/interactive_workflow/publication_handoff/models.py and handoff.py); the complete frozen CHGR schema family (human_governance_record.schema.json v1.1 plus its three sibling schemas and all six shared/*.schema.json files) and manifest.json; and the existing generic Layer-2 schema-validation infrastructure (src/pcae/schema_runtime/registry.py, validation.py), confirmed reusable unchanged for the CHGR family exactly as it already serves the Stage 3 Typed Authority Model family. Mapped all sixteen requirements (CHGR-REQ-194-209) to nine concrete implementation responsibilities (Sec.3.1-3.9 of the deliverable): manifest-sourced envelope construction, canonical identity/digest assignment across four artifacts, an explicit construction order resolving a forward-reference cycle, lifecycle_state assignment, authority_basis_claimed non-fabrication, assurance_level derivation, the three sibling artifacts' remaining fields, a new deterministic human-readable rendering function, and manifest/digest-utility reuse. Specified the fail-closed validation architecture in full (execution point -- inside the widened construction function, strictly before PublicationRecordStore.write_record; validation ordering; failure propagation via a new ChgrSchemaConformanceError subclass of the existing PublicationExecutionError hierarchy; diagnostic expectations; rollback expectations; publication refusal behavior; and CHGR-REQ-208's disclosure check specified precisely as a Python predicate distinct from JSON Schema validation). Designed integration with PublicationCoordinator.execute, record.py, storage.py, and the schema_runtime package without redesigning any existing ownership boundary (144G's forbidden-import boundary independently reconfirmed unbroken by this plan). Produced a concrete, atomic migration sequence (six steps, three independently landable with zero behavioral change plus one atomic widening step), a unit/integration/regression testing strategy, and a full risk assessment (R-1 through R-7). Independently discovered one implementation risk not previously disclosed by Phase 146A-146E: every _now_iso() helper in the repository (five independent copies across coordinator.py and interactive_workflow/**) emits a datetime.isoformat() string with a '+00:00' suffix, but the CHGR envelope schema's timestamp shape requires an explicit literal 'Z' suffix pattern -- every artifact this construction path produces would fail schema validation on every timestamp field unconditionally unless repaired; a minimum-necessary repair (normalize only at the CHGR construction boundary) is recommended but explicitly left as a disclosed, not-silently-resolved judgment call for the implementation phase, since this planning-only phase is not authorized to select an implementation detail on the contract's behalf. Also disclosed, with a resolving construction order, a genuine forward-reference cycle between human_governance_record.integrity_ref and governance_record_integrity.payload_digest, and left the four-artifact storage-layout choice (four files vs. one bundle) as a recommended-but-not-mandated judgment call. No Blocking findings. See docs/PHASE_146F_CHGR001_SCHEMA_ENVELOPE_IMPLEMENTATION_PLANNING.md. Verdict: IMPLEMENTATION PLAN COMPLETE WITH OBSERVATIONS.
